summary: Secondary wooden lookout cab on Purple Mountain, Yellowstone National Park; listed as gone; ranger fire patrols climbed the peak from 1931.

access.note: A trail listing describes a park hike to an overlook. No source read addresses the old lookout site on its own.

visit.trail_note: The trail listing says the hike ends at a 3.4-mile overlook and that visitors may find evidence of the old lookout site while scouting the area.

events.note: Ranger-naturalists stationed at Madison Junction were assigned to climb Purple Mountain three times a week for fire patrol; the climbs later opened to park visitors

evidence.quote: Originally, 16 were proposed in the Park, but 12 were actually constructed.

evidence.supports: three primary lookouts: Washburn 1921, Sheridan 1926, Holmes 1931
evidence.quote: The three primary lookouts were Mount Washburn, built in 1921

evidence.supports: Purple Mountain was a secondary lookout
evidence.quote: Secondary lookouts included Divide, Pelican Cone, Observation Peak, Purple Mountain, and Bunsen Peak.

evidence.supports: satellites and flyovers made many lookouts obsolete, in general
evidence.quote: Developments in fire-detection technologies with satellites and flyovers made many lookouts obsolete.

evidence.supports: secondary lookout station later built on the peak to supplement primary lookouts
evidence.quote: Later a "secondary" lookout station was built here to supplement the primary lookouts

evidence.supports: ranger-naturalists assigned fire patrol from 1931, three times a week
evidence.quote: were assigned fire patrol, three times a week climbing Purple Mountain to look for smoke

evidence.supports: park visitors allowed to join the climbs
evidence.quote: allowing park visitors to join the hike
ends at the 3.4-mile mark with a fine overlook

evidence.supports: visitors may find evidence of the old lookout site
evidence.quote: you may find evidence of the lookout

evidence.supports: NPS holds 1935 panoramic photos of Purple Mountain
NPS holds 2007 negatives of Purple Mountain
peak became one of the first ranger walks
evidence.quote: Purple Mountain became one of the first

notes_for_editor: No build date or removal date for the Purple Mountain cab appears in any source read; the trail listing says only that a secondary station was later built. The 1931 entry is patrol climbing, not a staffed lookout, so it is not coded as staffed. A Facebook post compiled with AI gives elevation 8,392 ft; not used, because firelookout.com gives 8,438 ft. The brief's access 'unknown' is now 'public' for the hike only. The brief's county 'Teton' matches firelookout.com.
